factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred Pacific temperature range for canary rockfish.
factors.value_notes: A 2009 Washington/Oregon trawl-logbook analysis found canary rockfish catches at bottom temperatures of 6.2-9.0 °C, but temperature was not significant in the fitted presence model after accounting for other variables and was highly correlated with bottom depth. These are bottom-trawl temperatures, not satellite SST, and do not validate the configured 7-15 °C SST range or 9-13 °C ideal.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, within prime Pacific depth zone for canary rockfish.
factors.value_notes: NOAA reports adult canary rockfish mainly at 160-820 feet (about 49-250 m), sometimes to 1400 feet. A Washington/Oregon trawl analysis found 57-307 m, with over 90% of catch tows between 57 and 199 m. The configured 20-150 m range and 22-145 m ideal omit much of the observed adult depth distribution, so depth is only partly supported and the ideal is not validated.
